## Root causes (all in `source/src/porespy/metrics/_funcs.py`)

The radial two-point correlation broke representation invariance and diverged from the documented definition in four compounding ways:

1. **`irfftn` silently truncated an odd-sized last axis** (`two_point_correlation`, `_funcs.py:1101`). Without `s=`, SciPy assumes the last axis is even-length, so the autocorrelation of the permuted volume (last axis 47) came out as 46 — and which axis is "last" depends entirely on array layout. Fixed with `s=im.shape`.

2. **Off-by-one radial distance origin** (`_radial_profile`, `_funcs.py:977,986`). After `ifftshift`, the autocorrelation's zero-lag sits at `(n+1)//2` along every axis (even and odd alike). `np.round(adj/2)` uses round-half-to-even, so for lengths ≡1 mod 4 (e.g. 45 → 22 instead of 23) the radial bins were measured around a wrong center — up to 0.14 deviation on this volume. Fixed with exact integer arithmetic `(adj + 1) // 2`.

3. **Radial sums truncated to `int64`** (`_get_radial_sum`, `_funcs.py:1018`). Truncating each float autocorrelation value before summing turned tiny, systematically-signed FFT round-off differences between representations into per-value flip differences, and biased every bin mean ~3e-5 below the true definition. Fixed to float64 accumulation.

4. **`probability` semantics contradicted the docstring** (`_funcs.py:1006`). Code returned the unit-normalized curve as `probability`, while the docstring defines `probability` as "scaled to the phase fraction at r = 0", documents `probability_normalized`, and says `pdf` is "Same as probability" (it wasn't, in code). Restored `probability_normalized = norm_autoc_radial` and `probability = norm_autoc_radial * pf`.
